entities.summary:
Chares of Athens (b. 400 BCE, Athens) was a prominent public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Athens. Known for his leadership in military campaigns and his ability to maintain social order, Chares of Athens played a crucial role in the governance of Athens during its most prosperous period.







 Chares of Athens implemented the 'Delian League', a military and economic alliance between Athens and its Greek city-states, which helped expand Athens' influence and secure its position as a dominant power in the Mediterranean.







 His administrative reforms aimed to modernize Athens' infrastructure, including the construction of a new canal at Piraeus, which significantly improved trade and commerce.
